definitions.explanation: A place in a body of water where the depth is shallow, such as a sandbar in the sea or a shallow stretch of a river that can be waded across.

examples.japanese: {浅瀬|あさせ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。

examples.english: The boat ran aground on a shoal.

examples.japanese: ⟦{川|かわ}→川：02186_kawa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{浅瀬|あさせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いて→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦{渡|わた}る→渡る：02441_wataru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: You can walk across the river at the shallows.

notes:
USAGE:
{浅瀬|あさせ} can refer to shallow areas in rivers, lakes, or the sea. It appears in the proverb {浅瀬|あさせ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{仇波|あだなみ} (much ado about nothing — literally "waves in the shallows"), describing people who make a fuss over trivial matters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {浅瀬|あさせ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{乗|の}り{上|あ}げる (to run aground on a shoal)
- {浅瀬|あさせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}る→渡る：02441_wataru⟧ (to wade across the shallows)
- {浅瀬|あさせ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧ (to play in the shallows)
